chunks: Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام was asked about the Imam praying while behind him were people lower than the place in which he was praying. He said:

“If the Imam is on something like a platform, or above their place, their salat is not valid. But if he is higher than them by a finger, or more, or less, when the elevation is due to a watercourse cut; and if the land is level and there is in one part of it an elevation, so the Imam stands in the elevated place and those behind him stand lower than him, while the land is level except that in one place it slopes downward, then there is no harm in it.”
And he was asked: If the Imam stands lower than the place of those who pray behind him? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

And he عليه السلام said: “If a man is above, on top of a house or otherwise, whether it is a platform or something else, and the Imam is praying on the ground and the Imam is lower than him, then the man may pray behind him and follow his salat, even if he is higher than him by a great amount.”

key_terms.الدُّكَّانِ: a raised platform or bench-like elevated place
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.يَقْتَدِيَ: to follow the Imam in salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Imam or the followers being at a higher or lower level in congregational salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on differences in elevation between the Imam and the followers in congregational salat. It indicates that the Imam standing on a distinctly raised platform above the followers invalidates their salat, while slight or naturally occurring elevation is excused, and it also permits followers to be above the Imam.
